subject: Hosted evaluation — quickstart suitability, endpoints, and rate caps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@luminalabs.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation — quickstart suitability, endpoints, and rate caps

Sara — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on so Lumina can decide whether to start with a Hosted API trial or aim straight for Dedicated/Private: 

- What we heard: primary goal is to validate inference quality and latency for your customer-facing summarization feature; production peak expected around 120 req/s (burst to 250) with most sessions ~60 tokens per response. EU data residency is a hard requirement for PII processing.
- Hosted quickstart we propose: sandbox endpoints in eu-west for integration + a warm canary in us-west for load testing. We can provision sandbox keys within 48 hours.
- Rate limits: Hosted trial defaults to per-route quotas with soft burst allowances; we can set a 150 qps soft limit and 250 qps burst for your trial account while we observe prefix/KV cache behavior.
- Decision guidance: if you need immediate EU residency and an SLA-backed contract for production, Dedicated (or Private VPC) will be necessary for go-live — but Hosted is often the fastest path to get realistic traffic profiling before committing.
- Next steps I need from you: the traffic sample export (anonymized), confirmation on whether EU region + encryption-at-rest/KMS controls are required for the trial, and a preferred time for a short call to review canary mapping.

Attaching short demo notes and a suggested traffic sample CSV template to make the traffic profile send easier.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: demo-notes-lumina.pdf (2 pages, highlights)
Attachment: lumina-traffic-sample.csv (CSV template)

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@luminalabs.com>

Cc: Patrick O'Neal <patrick@luminalabs.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 16:03:15 +0100
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation — quickstart suitability, endpoints, and rate caps

Thanks Dylan — useful recap. A few answers and notes from our side: 

- Traffic/export: attached is a redacted weekly export showing burst patterns (approx. peak 110–140 rps, hourly average ~35). We'll also try to export a full day with session lengths for next week.
- Residency & controls: We have a hard EU residency requirement for PII; non-PII inference can be routed through US. We are open to starting with Hosted (eu-west) for non-PII testing, but production PII handling will require Dedicated or Private with EU-only tenancy.
- SLA/Procurement: procurement will want to see SLA terms and a basic SOW; if the Hosted trial looks promising we expect a procurement conversation for Dedicated capacity within 6–8 weeks.
- Security contact: adding our security lead to the thread for questionnaire steps.

We can do the canary mapping call Tuesday 2 June 09:00 BST if that works.

Sara Chen
Head of Product — Lumina Labs

Attachment: lumina-security-contacts.vcf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@luminalabs.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2026 10:20:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation — quickstart suitability, endpoints, and rate caps

Sara — quick technical clarifications from the SE side so Lumina's engineering team can plan: 

- Regions: Hosted supports eu-west (single-tenant region for trial) and we can enforce EU-only data paths for the sandbox. For production PII, we can either provision Dedicated capacity in eu-west or deliver a Private VPC.
- Rate limits & quotas: Hosted trials use per-route token and request quotas. Example config for your trial: 150 qps route limit (sustained), 250 qps burst window (10s), and a per-token soft cost cap. We will monitor and propose adjustments after 72 hours of traffic.
- Endpoints/quickstart mapping: recommend two endpoints for the evaluation — /summarize-short (low-latency) and /summarize-long (higher token budget). We'll provide sample payloads and a test corpus.
- Caching & KV: prefix caching will likely reduce token load for repeated prompts; send us a 500–1,000 example prompt set so we can estimate cache hit-rate and projected token savings.

I'll attach the hosted-ratecard for reference and draft a short canary playbook for Tuesday's call. If Lumina wants, we can provision ephemeral sandbox keys today and push example client snippets for Node/Python.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: hosted-ratecard-v1.pdf
